newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China attacks Hong Kong's new container project.
newsitem.headline: China attacks Hong Kong's new container project.

text.p: A senior Chinese official on Sunday launched an attack on a plan by the Hong Kong government to build four new container terminals.
The plan to build Container Terminal 10 to 13 on Lantau, an outlying island in Hong Kong, was renewed after China and Britain reached an agreement on Container Terminal Nine last month.
The British colony will revert to Beijing's control on July 1 next year as a Special Administrative Region of China (SAR).

China has long been suspicious of any major infrastructure projects proposed by the British colonial government, worrying that they would drain the SAR government's coffer. It wants to be consulted before the Hong Kong government gives projects the go ahead.

Chen Zuo'er, Chinese member of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group that handles all the nitty-gritty of the handover arrangements, accused the Hong Kong government of being irresponsible since the plan was taken unilaterally without consulting Beijing.
"We are shocked when we heard about the news," Hong Kong TV and radio quoted Chen in Beijing as saying.
"What the Hong Kong government is doing now is irresponsible," he told reporters. "It is acting rashly. Do they think acting recklessly is good for Hong Kong? What is the purpose of it?"
Chen said the colonial administration should learn from the mistakes it made in the past over the new airport, rail, Container Port Nine and mobile phone licences.
These projects were only finalised recently after years of wrangling over the cost and tender procedure.
Analyst said the agreements showed signs of a warming in Sino-British relations after the two countries had squabbled over democracy, human rights and other issues since 1992.

The Chinese diplomat said Beijing did not oppose developments in the colony so long as they were beneficial to Hong Kong, and fitted in with a pattern of steady growth and the territory's economic future.
Hong Kong government officials were not immediately available for comment.
